multi_entity_precision.description: Precise multi-entity questions that should illustrate splitting/chunking and/or query decomposition

queries.query: Compare how the Academy handled the introduction of the Best Animated Feature category with the way the Best Original Score category was split and then merged again in the 1990s.
queries.expected_answer: The Best Animated Feature award was introduced at the 74th ceremony (2002) as a brand-new competitive category with eligibility rules: at least 70 minutes long, a significant number of animated characters, and at least 75 percent animation; a minimum of eight qualifying films had to be released in the year to allow three nominees, rising to five nominees if more than twelve films qualified. Before this, animated features such as Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Who Framed Roger Rabbit and Toy Story had only received Special Achievement Awards. By contrast, the score category was not created but divided: beginning with the 68th ceremony (1996) the music branch split Best Original Score into Best Dramatic Score and Best Musical or Comedy Score, seen as a response to Disney's dominance of the score and song categories; four years later the two scoring categories were merged back into one.

supporting_quotes.text: Beginning with this ceremony, AMPAS introduced a new competitive award that would honor animated feature films.

According to Academy communications director John Pavlik, the film must be at least 70 minutes in length, have a significant amount of animated characters, and be at least 75 percent animated in order to be qualified for consideration.

Prior to the introduction of this category, three Disney films (1937's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, 1988's Who Framed Roger Rabbit, and 1995's Toy Story) were all given Special Achievement Academy Awards.
Beginning with this ceremony, the AMPAS music branch divided the category of Best Original Score into two categories: Best Dramatic Score and Best Musical or Comedy Score.
This was seen as a response to the dominance of Walt Disney Feature Animation films in the Original Score and Original Song categories in recent years.
Four years later, the two scoring categories were merged back into one category.

queries.difficulty_notes: Genuine cross-document synthesis about category administration; no single article compares the two rule changes.
required_aspects: The Best Animated Feature award was introduced at the 74th ceremony (2002) as a brand-new competitive category with eligibility rules: at least 70 minutes long, a significant number of animated characters, and at least 75 percent animation
a minimum of eight qualifying films had to be released in the year to allow three nominees, rising to five nominees if more than twelve films qualified.
Before this, animated features such as Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Who Framed Roger Rabbit and Toy Story had only received Special Achievement Awards.

By contrast, the score category was not created but divided: beginning with the 68th ceremony (1996) the music branch split Best Original Score into Best Dramatic Score and Best Musical or Comedy Score, seen as a response to Disney's dominance of the score and song categories
four years later the two scoring categories were merged back into one.

queries.expected_answer: Brokeback Mountain won three Academy Awards — Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Original Score — but lost Best Picture to Crash, prompting accusations of homophobia and more than 800 supporters raising up to $26,000 for an advert in Daily Variety thanking the filmmakers. La La Land won six Oscars including Best Director and Best Actress from a record-tying fourteen nominations, but lost Best Picture to Moonlight after the envelope error, setting a record for most nominations without winning Best Picture. These figures reflect the sources' date and may be superseded.

queries.outcome_rationale: The fact exists in Harvard's article but is buried in a long alumni list; chunking isolates it, the graph reaches Bush through the shared Harvard node.
